WRITER SIDE (tools/runner) - the root fix, no command-string regex anywhere:
  layer 1 (exact): a dispatch runner exports MANAGENT_RUN_IDENTITY=<its identity> into the child
    before spawning. A runner in that child's tree whose identity EQUALS the marker is nested by
    construction. Equality, not presence: a leaf dispatched from inside a manager's console carries
    a different identity and owns its own dispatch slot (arm B4).
  layer 2 (structural, for a stripped environment and for the already-contaminated state): the
    identity has an un-finalized record (no exit/signal/end) whose pid is alive and whose process
    tree CONTAINS this process, per the same walker the orphan sweeper uses (_WALKER_FN). It scans
    the bare slot AND every archived attempt, because T650 displaces a live dispatch record into
    <id>.<N>.json - which is exactly the state the contamination leaves behind. Requiring
    containment, not mere liveness, is what makes pid reuse harmless.
  otherwise DISPATCH. Note the rule that was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: "identity came from
    MANAGENT_TASK_ID rather than --task-id therefore nested". bin/subagent sets env["MANAGENT_TASK_ID"]
    and does NOT pass --task-id (bin/subagent:798,834+), so that rule would have mislabelled every
    fleet dispatch. Also rejected: discriminating on the store's `dispatched` field (null for
    paste-line-launched consoles - it would blind the reaper to exactly the consoles that die
    silently) and any regex over `command` (the claimlint-green construction).
  A nested run writes untracked/runs/nested/<ident>.<pid>-<epoch>.json (a pure function of the
  record, so the launch write and the finalize write land in the same file) and does NOT call
  _begin_attempt, so it never rotates the dispatch slot. Every record now carries run_kind and
  run_kind_reason - the writer states the kind; no reader infers it.

READER SIDE (managent reap / resume) - the safety net:
  1. LIVENESS OVER RECENCY: any record for the identity (bare, archived attempt, or nested) that is
     un-finalized and whose pid is alive backs the row. This is what rescues rows whose dispatch
     record was already displaced by a pre-fix test run.
  2. THE DISPATCH RECORD, not the newest record: declared-nested records are never dispatch evidence.
  3. UNKNOWN, never ORPHAN, when records exist but none is a dispatch record - and UNKNOWN is not
     closable (isOrphanReap returns false; `reap --close` skips it; `resume` prints it as "? ... UNKNOWN").
  Every evidence line now names the record it read and its declared kind, e.g.
  "runner pid 99283 alive (record T895.1.json, kind undeclared, attempt 1, start ...)". Undeclared
  records (every record written before today) are read as dispatch candidates and LABELLED
  undeclared - they are never back-filled, because a back-filled record is a fabricated one.

RESIDUAL LIMITS, STATED PLAINLY:
  1. Records written before today carry no run_kind. They are read as dispatch candidates and
     labelled undeclared. A pre-existing nested record sitting in a bare slot can therefore still be
     read as a dispatch record - mitigated (not cured) by liveness-over-recency, which is what
     rescued T895/T890 above. Nothing is back-filled.
  2. A console the human launched by hand (no tools/runner ancestry, no marker, no live record for
     the identity) that runs tools/runner under its own task id still writes the bare slot as
     run_kind=dispatch. The store's `dispatched` field would discriminate it, and I rejected that:
     paste-launched rows have dispatched=null, so the reaper would go blind on exactly the consoles
     that die silently. What protects that case today is only the reader side (the row reads UNKNOWN
     or BACKED rather than ORPHAN whenever a live un-finalized record exists).
